clue.text: Traits which with care vary in styles

definitions.text: Traits which with care vary in styles

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked letters sit inside the word for styles

parts.note: chic means style or elegance, so styles in the plural are chics

indicators.note: vary asks for the letters of traits and care to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that personal traits are expressed differently according to how carefully one dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vary' mixes the two words into ARACTERIST; 'Traits' is both fodder and the sense, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics are distinguishing qualities or features, the same as traits.

clue.text: Actor to damage what might be called slim with food full of fat

parts.note: to mar something is to damage it

indicators.note: what might be called signals a word with the sound of the next word, not its spelling

parts.note: slim and lean both mean thin
your diet is the food you eat
rich food is heavy and full of fat

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to stay slim complains that rich, fatty food would damage their figure.
explanation.walkthrough: MARLENE DIETRICH was the German-born film star who is the theme of this puzzle; LENE is said like LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a celebrated film actress, the star whose films run through this grid.

clue.text: Enthusiastic response to "Eat fish in Indian city"?

indicators.note: in places the eating and the fish inside the name of the city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
taken as written
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Someone suggests going out to eat fish in an Indian city, and the reply is keen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the quoted suggestion as playful; 'in' places the meal inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a fine plan is a typical keen reply to a suggestion.

clue.text: Pants initially likely to need elastic

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of Pants

parts.note: liable, as in liable to happen, means likely

explanation.surface: A warning that underpants will probably need fresh elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underpants; here only its first letter, P, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable bends easily, as elastic material does; both mean flexible.

clue.text: See 19
Priest, with lots of animals in return for one from Tibet, to check a way to keep books

indicators.note: in places the priest and the animals inside the reversed beast
in return asks for the beast from Tibet to be read backwards

parts.note: the yak is the shaggy ox of Tibet
a lama is a Buddhist priest of Tibet
zoos hold lots of animals
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: A tangled story of a Tibetan priest and a menagerie exchanged for a yak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the Tibetan beast round to KAY; 'in' wraps it round the priest and animals. The Kalamazoo system is a loose-leaf bookkeeping method.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalamazoo system is a brand-name loose-leaf method of bookkeeping, so it is a way to keep accounts.

clue.text: Kidnap — old way to recruit sailors — in 2 picture

parts.note: to shanghai someone is to kidnap them, originally for service at sea
ex means former, so old
the press, or press gang, forced men into the navy

explanation.surface: A note that kidnapping was once how ships found crews, set in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old way to recruit sailors' looks like a gloss on 'Kidnap', but splits in two. '2' is MARLENE DIETRICH, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai Express is a 1932 film starring Marlene Dietrich, so it is one of her pictures.

clue.text: Islington's 2 picture when 5

parts.note: a London district's famous landmark which, with the colour from 5 added, becomes the title of the star's most famous film

explanation.surface: A cryptic note linking a north London landmark with a film of the star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angel is a well-known spot in Islington, north London; add BLUE (5) and you have The Blue Angel, Marlene Dietrich's breakthrough film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angel is the Islington landmark, and The Blue Angel is the Dietrich film it becomes with blue added.

clue.text: See articles with hate

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Advice to look at pieces of writing full of hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, which is a strong form of hating.

clue.text: Heat drug in front of radiator

parts.note: to grill food is to heat it under a grill
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone heats up a drug in front of the heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radiator' is the car radiator, not a room heater: a grille sits in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's grille is the grating placed in front of its radiator.

clue.text: Germany, the booze state

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze
Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A jibe that Germany is the country of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Alemaine is an archaic name for Germany, from the French Allemagne.

clue.text: Observe requirement of metre

definitions.meaning: to look over something closely, examining it
a line of verse must have the right rhythm to pass as metrical

explanation.surface: An instruction to notice what poetic rhythm demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look closely, and verse that scans keeps to its metre.

clue.text: Signalling start of the poem about 8, largely

indicators.note: start of means take only the opening letter of the
about tells us the poem goes round the cut-down angel

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: 8 is THE ANGEL; Raphael is one of the archangels

explanation.surface: A remark on how a poem about angels begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is THE ANGEL, here the archangel; 'largely' drops its last three letters, and 'about' wraps the poem round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegraphy is the sending of messages by telegraph, a system of signalling.

clue.text: Oppressed county cricket scene first

indicators.note: first says the cricket scene comes before the county in the answer

parts.note: a cricket ground is where the game is played
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone feels crushed by the county cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground down means worn down by harsh treatment, that is oppressed.

clue.text: Fencing with 4 weapons by theologian and comedian

parts.note: kendo is Japanese fencing with bamboo swords, pliable weapons, 4 being PLIABLE
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A comedian takes up fencing with bendy swords beside a theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN DODD was a much-loved British comedian from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd was a famous British stand-up comic with his tickling stick.

clue.text: Steal books and one gets caught — it's mechanical

parts.note: to rob is to steal
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A thief steals books and is caught, behaving like a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes behaving like a robot, that is in a mechanical way.

clue.text: Fruit needs good nurture

parts.note: a raisin is a dried grape, a fruit

explanation.surface: Advice that fruit needs proper care.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising children means bringing them up, which is nurture.

clue.text: See 22
Instrument heard with singular music in the shade

indicators.note: heard signals a word that sounds like the instrument

parts.note: a sax is a saxophone
the blues is a music; take it in the singular

explanation.surface: Someone plays sax with music in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: SAXE sounds like SAX; BLUES in the singular gives BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe blue is a light greyish-blue colour, a shade.

clue.text: Such as 2, king and queens with nothing on

parts.note: 2 is MARLENE DIETRICH, a film star
K is king in chess and cards
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen; ERS is several queens

explanation.surface: A film star, a king and some queens all go naked.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang meaning completely naked.

clue.text: The language has style

indicators.note: has signals that the answer is held inside the words the language

explanation.surface: A claim that a language possesses style.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a stylish verve.

clue.text: Kill, rejecting love, on right date — a profit for a 2 picture

indicators.note: rejecting asks for the love letter to be thrown out of the word for kill

parts.note: to destroy an animal is to kill it
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O
the Ides is a date in the Roman calendar, as in the Ides of March
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A tale of killing, ditching love, then making a profit on the right date.
explanation.walkthrough: DESTROY without O ('rejecting love') is DESTRY. Destry Rides Again (1939) starred Marlene Dietrich.
explanation.definitionFit: Destry Rides Again is a 1939 western with Marlene Dietrich, so one of her pictures.

clue.text: Bills for one with a tree

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill; two of them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A note of some bills plus one tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of trees and shrubs, the wattles.

clue.text: Renegotiated tenancy of northern fields with sheep about (or of life?)

indicators.note: about tells us the sheep goes round the fields

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: Northern fields with sheep about are leased afresh, giving them new life.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(or of life?)' is a nod to the phrase 'new lease of life'.
explanation.definitionFit: A new lease is a fresh tenancy agreement, as when one is renegotiated.
